mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in CPI inflation below 1% over the same quarter signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 101 for one quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction and related equities, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% for 2 months AND HOUST > 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for five consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as growth-sensitive sectors benefit.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
